missionPremise: OPS-24 P-219. Both PDF products drew every setback line, the envelope polygon and the buildable-area figure for 48021:34049 (1109 Pecan St, Bastrop, SF-1, a CORNER lot) from City of Bastrop Ordinance 2019-51, repealed 2026-04-14 by Ord. 2026-06 (B3 Code Repeal and Bastrop Development Code Adoption), while setbackRulesFact and the parcel_record rails served 30/10/30 with a 20 ft corner side cited to Ord. 2026-06. The facet was the correct side. Standing rulings the work rests on: MOST-CURRENT SOURCE WINS (operator 2026-09-11, _decisions/2026-09-11_setback_source_most_current_wins.md); THE LEDGER IS THE SERVING PATH, ATOMS ARE CANONICAL (operator 2026-09-11, one reader in hauska-engine/services/retrieval-api, OPS-23 §0); ENVELOPE DRAWN, FIGURE REFUSED (operator 2026-09-11, Ruling B reversed for the polygon only); A-148 (overseer 2026-09-14), which resolved F24 as ONE layer with unrefreshed numeric shortcut columns rather than two layers citing two ordinances.
completionPredicate: A customer exporting the feasibility study or the site plan for a Bastrop city SF-1 parcel reads the setbacks the current ordinance carries — 30/10/30 with a real corner-side line on a corner lot — cited to Ordinance 2026-06 with its effective date; no served setback value anywhere in the engine rests on a bastrop-per-parcel/* provenance where a ruled row exists to take over, and a CI check fails if one reappears; and the buildable-area figure on the covers either comes off the ruled table or is withheld with its reason stated. Evaluable by a stranger with: scripts/surface-probe.mjs --rows P-154 (the row whose predicate already compares panel, endpoint, MCP and PDF setbacks on this exact parcel), plus `node packages/engine-core/scripts/retire-bastrop-per-parcel-setback-authorship.mjs`.
scopeBasis: The dispatch scoped three build items (one setback source, honour side_corner, retire bastrop-per-parcel/*) plus D2's PDF half, in hauska-engine, with the retirement explicitly kept in THIS row. Three things were deliberately EXCLUDED rather than left unmentioned. (1) The per-parcel-record-only Bastrop districts, because the dispatch's own escalation falsifier fired on them — see `retirementIsPartial`. (2) R13/AMENDMENT 8, a standing ruling three controls assert and P-154 explicitly left alone; amending it is an operator call and is proposed here with evidence, not taken. (3) The situs fix, which was built, measured and reverted — it does not fix this parcel and it changes front-edge derivation product-wide in P-218's subject area. hauska-map, smartcity-os and smartcity-dashboards untouched.

Nothing on this path re-resolved it against a ruled table or the parcel_record rails.
packages/engine-core/src/site-plan/author.ts composeSitePlanModelForParcel() used that atom for the printed line AND handed it to prepareBoundaryEdgesForExport().

packages/engine-core/src/site-plan/prepare-boundary-edges-for-export.ts replaced EVERY stored per-edge setback with the atom's values whenever any of three triggers fired; for this parcel all three fired (stored sourceAdapter 'descriptor-fixture' is in the stale set, the jurisdiction is per-parcel-only, and edge 4 carries a refused road-class stamp).
The edges it discarded were already correct: get_smart_site 2026-09-15 reads boundaryEdgeFact as rear 30, side_corner 20, front 30, side 10, provenance 'district-setback-table'.

retirementIsPartial.statement: The retirement is complete for every district with a ruled corpus row and INCOMPLETE for Bastrop's per-parcel-record-only districts. This is named rather than narrated as a full retirement.
retirementIsPartial.measurement: Parcels_One_Click/FeatureServer/23, count of prop_id grouped by ZoneTypeClass over EVERY row in the layer, read live 2026-09-15. Denominator 16,751 rows. No zoning class 9,778 (58.4%); SF-1 2,496 (14.9%); PDD 1,995 (11.9%); GC 900 (5.4%); RR 689 (4.1%); MU 518 (3.1%); PI 241 (1.4%); IND 133 (0.8%); P/OS 1. SF-2 and SF-3 have ZERO rows on this layer. The per-parcel-record-only set (MU/GC/PDD/PI/IND/P-OS) is 3,788 rows, 22.6%.
retirementIsPartial.whyNotRetiredHere: The dispatch's own escalation falsifier — 'if you find the 2019 values are still authoritative for some district or some parcel, that is a bigger finding than this row and you escalate rather than continuing' — fired. Querying Zone_Types/FeatureServer/25 live 2026-09-15 shows the stale-numeric-column defect is NOT uniform: the SF rows are stale (text 30/10/30/20 vs numeric 25/5/25), but the GC row reads text 20/5/20 corner 10 and numeric 20/5/20, and the IND row reads text 25/20/25 corner 20 and numeric 25/20/25 — for those districts the columns the One Click join reads AGREE with the city's authoritative text. Blanket-retiring them would replace CORRECT values with an honest absence on roughly 1,274 GC+IND rows, which is a regression wearing a fix's clothes. MU is a third case again: text side '5 feet minimum; 0 feet allowed on shared/party-wall sides within a unified development; 10 feet where abutting RR or SF districts' against numeric SideSetback_ 0 — genuinely conditional language the flat model cannot hold, which is why the BDC's CORRECTION C omitted it in the first place.
retirementIsPartial.properFollowOn: A new adapter reading Zone_Types/FeatureServer/25 TEXT fields per district WITH their conditional language preserved, rather than flattened to a scalar. That is a build, not a flag flip, and it is not this row.

cornerSide.whatWasMissing: The engine had no corner-side axis above the per-edge layer. SitePlanSetbackModel carried front/side/rear; NotSpecifiedAxes carried front/side/rear; and prepare-boundary-edges-for-export's own comment said it outright: 'side + side_corner share the "side" not-specified axis (SetbackDisplay NotSpecifiedAxes carries no separate corner flag)'. So a corner axis with no published value silently degraded to the interior-side number, and the persisted atom for this parcel carried no sideCornerFt at all.
cornerSide.whatWasBuilt: cornerFt is a first-class axis through the resolver, the per-edge refresh, the site model and the printed summary line, with its own sideCorner silent-axis flag. A district that publishes NO corner value now yields an ABSENCE on that edge with a stated reason, never the interior-side number under a corner label.
cornerSide.provenOnTheCornerLot: 48021:34049, the parcel the dispatch named. Regenerated read-only: the sheet draws SIDE (CORNER) 20' and the per-edge segments read rear=30 | side=10 | side_corner=20 | front=30 | side=10.

regeneratedArtifacts.preRegisteredBand: CP1 pre-registered 16,300-16,800 sq ft and 54-56% for the corrected envelope, before any code was written. The composer's own locally-derived figure came out at 16,767 sq ft, INSIDE the band. The percentage came out at 56.5%, 0.5 points ABOVE the predicted band, and the reason is stated rather than smoothed: the harness ring (the city One Click layer) measures 29,652 sq ft against the product's 29,989 sq ft, a 337 sq ft smaller denominator. Both numbers are reported, not just the one that matched.
regeneratedArtifacts.honestLimits: This is a faithful exercise of the setback resolution, the per-edge refresh, the label path and the figure gate on real inputs. It is NOT a full production render: the DEM, the flood read, the aerial imagery and the attaching road nodes were stubbed, and the ring came from the city layer rather than the TxGIO ring the production resolver uses. A regenerated FEASIBILITY pdf was not produced locally — composeParcelReportFacts needs the substrate store and live fact resolvers — but the feasibility sheets read the SAME model.setback and summary.printedBuildable fields the site plan does (pdf/feasibility.ts:250-254 and its narrative validator both key on printedBuildable), so the setback row and the cover figure move with them by construction rather than by a second implementation.

buildableFigurePolicy.decisionTaken: The figure prints only when the buildable-envelope atom backing it describes the envelope this sheet actually drew. It is refused, with its reason on the sheet, when (a) the setback values this export followed differ from the ones the persisted setback-rule atom carries — i.e. the envelope was derived from a source the sheet has stopped following — or (b) the setback layer is honest-absent, so there is no envelope for a figure to describe. The POLYGON still draws in both cases, which is exactly what Ruling B reversed for the polygon only.
bothOptionsStated: A — print it, off the ruled table, on all three surfaces. Requires lifting buildable_area and lot_coverage_pct from DERIVED_FIGURES_POLICY, backing the figure with a re-baked envelope atom, and making panel, facets endpoint and both PDFs read that one atom. Cost: touches the wire policy and hauska-map, outside this row's repo, and runs against the operator's 2026-09-11 ruling as it stands.
B — withhold it wherever it cannot be shown to describe the drawing. Cost: a number a buyer currently sees disappears from the cover until the envelope is re-baked.
buildableFigurePolicy.whyB: Option B, and the reason is not squeamishness: the figure as it stood was not merely barred, it was WRONG. The PDF printed its own dimensions — 'an envelope roughly 131 by 158 ft at its widest' — and 181.06 - 25 - 25 = 131.06 while 168.30 - 5 - 5 = 158.30, so the figure is arithmetically the repealed setbacks. Printing a re-derived number instead would require minting an envelope atom, which is a write to a serving store and this program's own operator stop point.
buildableFigurePolicy.whatChangedFromCP1AndWhy: CP1 planned a numeric-agreement tolerance (refuse when the atom's area and the sheet's own offset-ring area differ by more than 2%). Implemented, it broke three existing controls, one titled '(a) prints exactly ONE buildable figure and ONE consistent percent on every surface when the atom-backed (warm) and local figures differ'. Reading it showed the divergence is that control's METHOD — it sets the atom figure 4,000 sq ft away from the local derive precisely so that a leak of the local number is unmistakable. A tolerance check would have destroyed the instrument that proves one figure prints per document. The gate was rebuilt on PROVENANCE instead and all three controls pass untouched. Two figures differing is P-159's method; two figures resting on different setback law is P-219's defect.
buildableFigurePolicy.notWithholdingByOmission: The policy was written into CP1 before a line of code was changed, and the refusal carries a sentence on the sheet rather than leaving a blank.
buildableFigurePolicy.escalatedAnyway: The facets endpoint's own buildableAreaSqFt (19,052, with buildableAreaPct 63.5) lives in hauska-map and is untouched by this row. Until it is routed, the facets endpoint still serves a 25/5/25-derived figure beside its own corrected 30/10/30/20 setbacks block — the endpoint disagreeing with itself. The surface probe independently flagged the same thing as FIGURE-IN-PAYLOAD on both probed parcels.

proposalsForTheOperator.evidence: A-148 established, and this lane re-verified live 2026-09-15, that the chart and the city's own authoritative layer TEXT agree exactly for SF-1 (30/10/30/20) and RR (50/20/50/20), and that only the unrefreshed numeric shortcut columns dissent. proposalsForTheOperator.costOfNotDoingIt: A Bastrop city parcel whose reader read fails now honest-absents its setback layer instead of falling back to the ordinance. That is honest and is strictly better than the repealed numbers, but it is a degradation the amendment would remove.

The amendment was written, it made those three controls fail, and it was reverted with the reasoning recorded at the decision point in getSetbackTableForZoning.

falsifier: Pre-registered at CP1 before any code was written. (1) Engine agrees with the facet but bastrop-per-parcel/* still answers — NOT TRIPPED where a ruled row exists: proven by decline in two test files and by a CI instrument itself proved able to fail on the real exit code; PARTIALLY OPEN for the per-parcel-record-only districts, which is escalated and encoded as the instrument's one stated exclusion rather than left silent. (2) Tested a non-corner lot only — NOT TRIPPED: 48021:34049 is the corner lot, it is the test parcel, and the regenerated sheet draws SIDE (CORNER) 20'. (3) Buildable figure disappeared without a stated policy — NOT TRIPPED: stated in CP1 before the code, and the refusal carries its reason on the sheet. (4) Numbers match but cannot say WHICH source — NOT TRIPPED: the sheet prints the source label, the ordinance URL and the effective date, and the provenance row reads bastrop_tx/bdc-2026-adopted/14.02.003. (5) 2019 values still authoritative somewhere — FIRED, and handled by escalating rather than continuing through it.
contradicted: Four things this lane believed and then disproved. (a) That a secret mount was this row's operator stop point — the code said RETRIEVAL_API_URL/KEY were unmounted; gcloud says they are mounted, and the stale comment was corrected at source. (b) That the buildable figure could be gated on numeric agreement — implemented, it destroyed P-159's leak-detection control, and the gate was rebuilt on provenance. LESSON: A freshness gate can become the staleness. The 2026-08-05 edge-role gate was built to stop a stale setback reaching the sheet and, once the atom it trusted became the stale side, was the thing injecting one. When a guard names a specific trusted source, that name is the thing to re-verify, not the guard's logic.

Before replacing a behaviour a test asserts, read why the test asserts it. A numeric-divergence gate looked obviously right and would have destroyed P-159's leak-detection control, whose METHOD is to make the two figures diverge. The control's intent was in its title.

`pnpm -r` stops at the first failing package, so a filtered console read can hide a whole service's results. CI found six failures in services/engine-api that the local run had actually surfaced and the output filter had cut. Read the exit code, not the lines you chose to print.

A mock must export every name the module under test imports, or the import fails before any assertion and the route's error mapper turns it into a plausible-looking domain refusal (422 setback_rule_missing). The failure will not look like a mock problem.
